verdict.rationale: Bitwarden calls itself 'the most trusted open source password manager', and community users confirm the clients are open source; one says they chose it specifically to avoid closed-source clients. A user also thanks Bitwarden for relicensing back to a Free/Open license after the SDK controversy. However, no first-party doc points to the client-app source repositories, licenses or review/audit process, so client-level inspectability is only implied. Missing for 10: first-party docs naming the client-app source repositories and licenses, evidence of community or independent code review of the seed-handling code, and clear current licensing status of the client SDK.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the client apps are open source, so the code handling my seeds can be inspected and community-reviewed

citations.quote: The most trusted open source password manager for passwords, passkeys, and secrets
